obligations.findingAsRecorded: The service mechanics are right and the objection clock is wrong in a way that can mislead a felony-class petitioner. The packet led with a flat "The prosecuting attorney has 30 days to object", demoted the profile's class-keyed rule to "the longer window MAY apply to you", and then sent a statutory question to the clerk.

recordIRelyOn.whatItShows: rules.service is the identical string "Serve the prosecuting attorney within three days of filing. The prosecuting attorney has 30 days to object." on 11 of the 12 Arkansas tracks — measured in this lane: every track except ar-preadjudication-probation, whose rules.service is "none". ar-felony-seal carries it, and the same repository puts the felony window at 90 days.
recordIRelyOn.whyItDoesNotDecideThisRoute: DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A3: holding is per FACT, not per document. A sentence provably wrong on a sibling track it is attached to is state-level boilerplate and addresses no route's objection window.

recordIRelyOn.whatItShows: The rule stated class-keyed, three times: ruleText "Prosecutor objection window — misdemeanor 30 days Receipt / filing of petition" (line 2050) and "Prosecutor objection window — felony 90 days Receipt / filing of petition" (line 2063), and in filingDestinationRules / serviceAndNoticeRules "The prosecutor has 30 days (misdemeanor) or 90 days (felony) to file a notice of opposition stating reasons."
recordIRelyOn.whyItReachesThisExactRoute: The rule is self-applying on the delivered instrument. Paragraph 1 of the petition in this packet prints "A Class _____ [_] felony [_] misdemeanor" and the participant supplies the class, so the packet does not have to choose a limb — it has to state the rule and let the participant's own entry decide it. Confirmed against the delivered raster, not only the field census.

whatIChanged.change: The objection-window paragraph now states the class rule AS the rule, quotes both limbs from the profile with the profile's path, and says the window runs from the filing of the petition. The sentence "ask the clerk of the court where you file which window that court runs" is deleted and replaced with the reason it was wrong: the window is statutory and identical in every Arkansas court, so a clerk cannot answer it. The flat "The prosecuting attorney has 30 days to object" half of the manifest quotation is removed from the three-day paragraph, which now quotes only the half that carries the service deadline.
whatIChanged.boundedness: One paragraph plus one quotation trim. No other section, no other family, no shared code.

reMeasurement.textNowDelivered: **Then expect an answer, or expect silence — and how long you wait depends on the class you tick in paragraph 1.** … states the rule twice and states it class-keyed both times: **"Prosecutor objection window — misdemeanor 30 days | Receipt / filing of petition"** and **"Prosecutor objection window — felony 90 days | Receipt / filing of petition"** … **tick misdemeanor and the window is 30 days; tick felony and it is 90 days.** Count from the filing of the petition. Do not ask the clerk which window applies — the window is set by statute and is the same in every Arkansas court, and a clerk's office cannot shorten or lengthen it.

recordIRelyOn.whyItCountsAsHeld: DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A2, whatCountsAsHeld: "the compiled state profile for the family's jurisdiction" — listed unconditionally, and deliberately so. This route's census does NOT enumerate the profile as a requiredSourceId (measured in this lane against packet-family-build-worklist.json; the sibling arrest route does), which is precisely the case A2 was written to settle.
recordIRelyOn.whyItReachesThisExactRoute: A3 bounds A2: a record answers only the route it addresses. The link is on the delivered instrument, not inferred. The order in this packet decrees sealing "pursuant to A.C.A. §16-90-1405" and directs the agencies to comply with "A.C.A. §16-90-1413" — both Act 1460 sections — which I read off the delivered order's page 2 raster in this lane. The same profile labels § 16-90-1405 "Situation B — Misdemeanor convictions (§ 16-90-1405)" and lists this exact instrument pair among the Act 1460 forms at line 2444. The fee rule is keyed to Act 1460 sealing; this filing is an Act 1460 sealing.

theResidualTheVerifierRaised.raised: The profile's $0 line does not name DWI/BWI in the fee sentence itself, and § 5-65-111 is a separate eligibility scheme, so a counsel reader could hold that this route carries its own cost.
theResidualTheVerifierRaised.howIAnsweredIt: Measured, not waved past. Ark. Code Ann. § 5-65-111 appears NOWHERE in AR-arkansas.json (zero occurrences); § 16-90-1405 appears thirteen times. On the delivered instruments, § 5-65-111(b)(1)/(c)(1) is cited only in paragraph 7 as the ten-year waiting-period condition, while the operative sealing is ordered under § 16-90-1405. So § 5-65-111 supplies eligibility, not a filing scheme.
theResidualTheVerifierRaised.andItIsStatedToTheParticipant: The instruction carries the limit in its own words rather than hiding it: "the profile's $0 sentence does not itself repeat the words 'DWI' or 'BWI', and it is the Act 1460 chain above, not the fee sentence's own wording, that carries it to this route." A counsel reader who disagrees can see exactly which link to dispute.
